claims.text: Combining machine learning with empirical knowledge can be used to predict phase stability in high-entropy alloys.
Combining machine learning with empirical knowledge can be used for microstructure refinement in high-entropy alloys.
Combining machine learning with empirical knowledge can be used for property optimization in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method applies to as-cast or additively manufactured high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning algorithms and empirical knowledge can jointly predict and optimize phase stability.
Machine-learning algorithms and empirical knowledge can jointly predict and optimize microstructure.
The proposed approach is applicable across varied temperatures, atmospheres, and processing routes.
Configurational entropy is a relevant mediator or descriptor of phase stability in high-entropy alloys.
Atomic size difference is a relevant mediator or descriptor in high-entropy-alloy phase prediction.
Lattice distortion mediates phase stability or microstructure refinement in high-entropy alloys.
Machine learning predicts phase stability and microstructure.
Empirical knowledge optimizes processing conditions and alloy composition.
The proposed method produces improved phase stability relative to conventional trial-and-error development.
The proposed method produces a refined microstructure relative to conventional trial-and-error development.
The proposed method produces optimized mechanical properties relative to conventional trial-and-error development.
Conventional trial-and-error methods provide the baseline for alloy development.
The approach is limited by the availability of high-quality data and the complexity of high-entropy-alloy systems.
Machine-learning prediction accuracy and the transferability of empirical knowledge across different high-entropy-alloy systems are uncertain.
A controlled comparison against conventional methods can test whether the proposed approach improves phase stability, microstructure, and mechanical properties.
Failure to improve phase stability and microstructure relative to conventional methods would falsify the hypothesis.
